item.title: Elder Nun Sumānā: O that elder nun, Lie down happily, Covered in your robe, Made by yourself. Your greed is calmed, You are cooled, at…
item.description:
Elder Nun Sumānā:

O that elder nun,
Lie down happily,
Covered in your robe,
Made by yourself.
Your greed is calmed,
You are cooled, at peace.

From: Therīgāthā 1.16

item.title: When you gather together, bhikkhus, there are two things to be done: discussing the Dhamma or maintaining noble silence." Then the Blessed One, having understood…
item.description:
When you gather together, bhikkhus, there are two things to be done: discussing the Dhamma or maintaining noble silence." Then the Blessed One, having understood the meaning of this, on that occasion uttered this inspired utterance:

One who lives without worldly work,
Light, desiring welfare,
With faculties restrained,
Fully liberated,

Homeless, without 'I-making',
Without sensual desire, having slain Māra,
Such a bhikkhu
Lives alone.

From: Udāna 3.9

item.title: Elder Khitaka: My body is light, touched by great joy and bliss. Like cotton blown by the wind, my body floats.
item.description:
Elder Khitaka:

My body is light, touched by great joy and bliss.
Like cotton blown by the wind, my body floats.

From: Theragāthā 1.104

item.title: There are these four inconceivable things, bhikkhus, that should not be speculated about; one who speculates about them would be subject to madness and distress.…
item.description:
There are these four inconceivable things, bhikkhus, that should not be speculated about; one who speculates about them would be subject to madness and distress. What four? The sphere of a Buddha, bhikkhus, is inconceivable; one who speculates about it would be subject to madness and distress. The sphere of one in meditation, bhikkhus, is inconceivable; one who speculates... distress. The result of kamma, bhikkhus, is inconceivable; one who speculates... distress. Speculation about the world, bhikkhus, is inconceivable; one who speculates would be subject to madness and distress.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.77

item.title: Furthermore, Meghiya, a bhikkhu dwells energetic and strenuous, abandoning unwholesome states, arousing wholesome states, steadfast, resolute, not discarding the burden regarding wholesome states. This is…
item.description:
Furthermore, Meghiya, a bhikkhu dwells energetic and strenuous, abandoning unwholesome states, arousing wholesome states, steadfast, resolute, not discarding the burden regarding wholesome states. This is the fourth quality, Meghiya, that leads to the maturity of the unripe liberation of mind. Furthermore, Meghiya, a bhikkhu has wisdom, possessing wisdom that penetrates arising and passing away, with the noble penetration leading to the complete destruction of suffering. This is the fifth quality, Meghiya, that leads to the maturity of the unripe liberation of mind.

From: Udāna 4.1

item.title: Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu takes hold of the hem of my robe and follows right behind me, placing his feet where my feet have been,…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu takes hold of the hem of my robe and follows right behind me, placing his feet where my feet have been, yet if he has craving for sensual pleasures, strong greed, a hateful mind, evil thoughts, forgetfulness, lack of clear comprehension, unconcentrated, with distracted mind and loose faculties — that one is far from me, and I am far from him. Why is that? That bhikkhu does not see the Dhamma. Not seeing the Dhamma, he does not see me.

Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu lives a hundred leagues away, yet if he has no craving for sensual pleasures, no strong greed, no hateful mind, no evil thoughts, is mindful, clearly comprehending, concentrated, one-pointed, with restrained faculties — that one is close to me, and I am close to him. Why is that? That bhikkhu sees the Dhamma. Seeing the Dhamma, he sees me.

Though one may follow at the heel,
But full of desire and discontent,
Behold such a person: truly far, far away,
Far between one with craving and one without,
Far between the calm and the uncalm,
Far between one with greed and one who has abandoned greed.

Having fully known the Dhamma,
The wise one who knows the Dhamma,
Like a windless lake, unshaken, calm.
Behold such a person: truly near, very near,
Near between one without craving and one without craving,
Near between the calm and the calmed,
Near between the non-greedy and the one who has abandoned greed.

From: Itivuttaka 92

item.title: Elder Nāgasamāla: Adorned, wearing fine clothes, wearing garlands, fragrant, With sandalwood scent, in the crowd, on the main road, A dancer was dancing, moving to…
item.description:
Elder Nāgasamāla:

Adorned, wearing fine clothes, wearing garlands, fragrant,
With sandalwood scent, in the crowd, on the main road,
A dancer was dancing, moving to the music.

I entered the city for alms, passing by, I saw her —
Adorned, wearing fine clothes, setting the snare of death.

Then I reflected wisely, arousing right thought.
The danger appeared; disgusted, I became established.

And my mind was liberated — such is the Dhamma-nature.
I have attained the three knowledges; done is the Buddha's teaching.

From: Theragāthā 4.1
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: Elder Bhadda: I was an only child, loved by father and mother. Through many rites and observances, I was obtained with entreaties. Out of compassion…
item.description:
Elder Bhadda:

I was an only child, loved by father and mother.
Through many rites and observances, I was obtained with entreaties.

Out of compassion for me, wishing for my happiness,
Both my father and mother led me to the Buddha.

'This son of ours, obtained with great difficulty,
Raised with delicacy, nurtured and cared for,
We respectfully offer him to you, O savior,
To serve as your attendant, to serve the conqueror.'

The Teacher accepted me, saying to Ānanda:
'Let him go forth; he will become virtuous.'

After the Teacher had me go forth,
The conqueror then entered the monastery.
Before the sun rose, my mind was liberated.

Then my Teacher, to complete the task,
From silent meditation, stood up and called me:
'Come, Bhadda.' Thus I received full ordination.

From birth, at seven years, I received full ordination.
I have attained the three knowledges — O Dhamma, good Dhamma-nature!

From: Theragāthā 7.3

item.title: Just as rust is born from iron, And, born, eats away the iron, So excessive gain and honor lead One's own deeds to a bad…
item.description:
Just as rust is born from iron,
And, born, eats away the iron,
So excessive gain and honor lead
One's own deeds to a bad destination.

Among these defilements,
Ignorance is the worst.
Bhikkhu, abandon that defilement,
Become free from defilements.

Easy is life for the shameless,
One who is bold as a crow,
One who is backbiting and boastful,
One who is reckless and defiled.

Difficult is life for the modest,
One who always seeks purity,
One who is unassuming and humble,
One who is pure and bright.

From: Dhammapada 235-255

item.title: There are these three kinds of persons, bhikkhus, who appear in the world. What three? Here, bhikkhus, a person accumulates harmful bodily formations, accumulates harmful…
item.description:
There are these three kinds of persons, bhikkhus, who appear in the world. What three? Here, bhikkhus, a person accumulates harmful bodily formations, accumulates harmful verbal formations, accumulates harmful mental formations. Having accumulated harmful bodily formations, harmful verbal formations, harmful mental formations, he is reborn in a harmful world. Being reborn in a harmful world, harmful contacts touch him. Touched by harmful contacts, he experiences harmful feelings, exclusively painful, like beings in hell. Here, bhikkhus, a person accumulates non-harmful bodily formations ... non-harmful mental formations. Having accumulated non-harmful bodily formations ... non-harmful mental formations, he is reborn in a non-harmful world. Being reborn in a non-harmful world, non-harmful contacts touch him. Touched by non-harmful contacts, he experiences non-harmful feelings, exclusively pleasant, like the Subhakiṇha devas. Here, bhikkhus, a person accumulates both harmful and non-harmful bodily formations ... both harmful and non-harmful mental formations. Having accumulated both harmful and non-harmful bodily formations ... both harmful and non-harmful mental formations, he is reborn in a world that is both harmful and non-harmful. Being reborn in a world that is both harmful and non-harmful, contacts that are both harmful and non-harmful touch him. Touched by them, he experiences feelings that are both harmful and non-harmful, a mixture of pleasure and pain, like humans, some devas, and some beings in the lower realms. These three kinds of persons, bhikkhus, appear in the world.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.23
